story.tasks:
- [ ] **T1 – Implement CLI user commands** - [ ] Create `src/cli/commands/users/index.ts` as the users subcommand with nested commands. - [ ] Implement `list.ts`: call `UserService.list/search`, output table or JSON. - [ ] Implement `get.ts`: call `UserService.get`, output full user details. - [ ] Implement `create.ts`: call `UserService.create`, output created user. - [ ] Implement `update.ts`: call `UserService.update`, output updated user. - [ ] Implement `delete.ts`: call `UserService.delete`, with confirmation prompt. - [ ] Implement `reset-password.ts`: prompt for password, call `UserService.resetPassword`. - [ ] Implement `credentials.ts`: list credentials, with --delete option.
- [ ] **T2 – Create CLI utilities and wire up main entry** - [ ] Create `src/cli/utils/output.ts` for table/JSON formatting helpers. - [ ] Update `src/cli/index.ts` to register the users subcommand and validate connection on startup. - [ ] Ensure CLI outputs clean, human-readable errors (not raw stack traces).
- [ ] **T3 – Tests** - [ ] Add Vitest tests for CLI commands verifying argument parsing and output formatting. - [ ] Test table output includes expected columns. - [ ] Test JSON output is valid JSON matching domain types.

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
1. **CLI command surface** - Given CLI is installed When I run `kc users --help` Then I see available subcommands: list, get, create, update, delete, reset-password, credentials
2. **List users command** - `kc users list [--search <term>] [--max <n>] [--json]` - Lists users in table format (default) or JSON - Table shows: id, username, email, enabled
3. **Get user command** - `kc users get <id> [--json]` - Shows full user details
4. **Create user command** - `kc users create --username <u> [--email <e>] [--firstName <f>] [--lastName <l>] [--json]` - Creates user, outputs created user
5. **Update user command** - `kc users update <id> [--username <u>] [--email <e>] [--enabled <bool>] [--json]` - Updates user attributes
6. **Delete user command** - `kc users delete <id> [--force]` - Deletes user, asks confirmation unless --force
7. **Reset password command** - `kc users reset-password <id> [--temporary]` - Prompts for new password (no echo) - Sets password
8. **Credentials command** - `kc users credentials <id> [--json]` - Lists user's credentials (passkeys, OTP, etc.) - `kc users credentials <id> --delete <credId> [--force]` - Removes credential with confirmation

doc.title: Architecture — keycloak-commander
doc.snippet: CLI uses citty (ADR-004): `runMain(defineCommand({ subCommands: { users: () => import('./commands/users') } }))`. Commands follow pattern: delegate to service layer, format output (table/JSON), handle errors cleanly.

doc.title: Architecture — keycloak-commander
doc.snippet: Commands use citty's `defineCommand` with args, call service methods (e.g., `getUserService()`), format output via utils (`printTable`, `printJson`). Table columns: id, username, email, enabled. JSON mode for scripting.

doc.title: Architecture — keycloak-commander
doc.snippet: CLI commands: kebab-case (e.g., `reset-password`). Functions: camelCase. Exit codes: 0 (success), 1 (error), 2 (not found).

story-context.constraints: - **CLI Framework**: MUST use citty's `defineCommand` and `subCommands` pattern per ADR-004 - **Service Delegation**: Commands contain ONLY argument parsing and output formatting — NO business logic - **Service Access**: MUST obtain UserService via `getUserService()` factory, never instantiate directly - **Naming**: Command names use kebab-case (e.g., `reset-password`), function names use camelCase - **Output Formats**: - Default: Human-readable table with columns: id, username, email, enabled - JSON mode: Valid JSON matching User domain types exactly - **Error Handling**: - Catch IdentiKeyError, display error code + message + suggestions - Exit codes: 0 (success), 1 (general error), 2 (not found) - No raw stack traces in production mode - **Confirmation Prompts**: Destructive ops (delete, delete-credential) require confirmation unless --force flag - **Password Input**: reset-password must use no-echo terminal input for security - **Connection Validation**: CLI must validate Keycloak connection on startup before executing commands - **Testing**: Mock UserService to test command logic in isolation (no real Keycloak calls in unit tests)

tests.standards: Use Vitest for unit tests co-located with source files. Mock UserService using Vitest mocks. Test command arg parsing, output formatting (table/JSON), error handling. Verify citty correctly routes to command handlers. Test edge cases: empty results, invalid IDs, network errors.
tests.locations: - src/cli/commands/users/*.spec.ts — CLI command tests - src/cli/utils/output.spec.ts — Output formatter tests - Tests should NOT make real Keycloak API calls (use mocked UserService)
tests.ideas: AC1: Test `kc users --help` shows all subcommands AC2: Test list command parses --search, --max, --json flags; verify table has 4 columns AC3: Test get command with valid ID returns full user; invalid ID shows error AC4: Test create command with --username required, optional --email AC5: Test update command modifies fields AC6: Test delete command prompts confirmation, respects --force flag AC7: Test reset-password prompts for input AC8: Test credentials command lists credentials, --delete removes specific credential - Test printTable formats User array correctly - Test printJson outputs valid JSON - Test printError shows IdentiKeyError code and message - Test command exits with code 2 for USER_NOT_FOUND errors
